sections.title: 2. Who the exam is for
sections.html:
As a candidate for this Microsoft Certification, you design and configure AI-enhanced sales solutions by using Dynamics 365 Sales, Copilot in Dynamics 365 Sales, and agent capabilities to help sellers work more efficiently throughout the lead-to-cash process. You translate business requirements into practical seller workflows enhanced with conversational intelligence, predictive insights, guided automation, and secure data access.

In this role, you work closely with sales, operations, and IT stakeholders to help ensure that solutions align with revenue goals and process optimization.

You perform the following design and implementation tasks:

  • Configure Dynamics 365 Sales core features.
  • Deploy, manage, and monitor agents in Sales.
  • Implement collaboration features.
  • Tailor AI-powered intelligence features.

It is highly recommended that candidates complete training in intermediate-level Microsoft Power Platform configuration before taking this certification exam. Additionally, you must have functional knowledge of:

  • Interpreting an organization’s sales processes and seller experience.
  • Building and extending model-driven apps.
  • Building Power Automate cloud flows.

Source: Official study guide (audience profile), updated 2026-10-16.

sections.title: 4. How to read the skills measured
sections.html:
• The bullets illustrate how a skill is assessed; related topics may appear (Microsoft's own note in the study guide). Treat each bullet as a heading for everything around it.
  • Most questions cover generally available (GA) features, but Preview features can appear when they are commonly used. Where the documentation labels something preview, retired or renamed, this guide says so.
  • Expect scenario questions (pick the right setting, path, role or sequence for a requirement) and decision questions (X versus Y). Exact names, menu paths and limits matter.
  • Case studies present a business scenario followed by several questions. Read the requirements and constraints once, then answer every question against them. Microsoft's break rules differ inside case-study and problem/solution sets.

sections.title: 1.1 Configure Sales
sections.html:
Skills measured: Evaluate prerequisites for deploying Sales • Configure mailboxes • Set up and configure business process flows • Configure the timeline • Evaluate options for importing and exporting data • Examine the Sales security model • Configure Microsoft 365 functionality, including Microsoft Teams, SharePoint, Outlook, and OneDrive. Practice by standing up one Sales environment end to end: create it with Dynamics 365 apps enabled, install Sales Hub, sync a mailbox, build and activate a business process flow, tune a timeline, import a CSV, and connect SharePoint, OneDrive and Teams chat.

Evaluate prerequisites for deploying Sales

Dynamics 365 Sales runs on Dataverse and its apps are model-driven apps, so a deployment starts by checking the environment, the license and the Microsoft 365 services you plan to integrate.

AreaWhat the documentation requires
EnvironmentA production or sandbox environment created with a Dataverse database and Enable Dynamics 365 apps = Yes at creation. You need a Dynamics 365 license to choose Yes, and if you skip it you cannot change it later or install Dynamics 365 apps in that environment. Creating an environment with a database needs at least 1 GB of available database capacity. Create it as a Dynamics 365 or Power Platform admin: Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > New. The Currency you pick there is the base currency.
License and appSales Professional → Sales Professional app. Sales Enterprise or Sales Premium → Sales Hub app (pre-installed with the Dynamics 365 Sales Embedded Package). Team Member license → Sales Team Member app. Use only the app your license includes, even when another one is visible; in a Sales Professional environment hide Sales Hub. Microsoft Relationship Sales (Sales Enterprise plus LinkedIn Sales Navigator) is not available for direct purchase: buy through a Microsoft representative or partner.
InstallPower Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > the environment > Resources > Dynamics 365 apps > Install app (tenant view: Manage > Dynamics 365 Apps). Then confirm the app in Power Apps, share it, assign licenses in the Microsoft 365 admin center, and assign security roles.
Client and networkBrowsers and operating systems follow the Power Apps list. The embedded Teams dialer follows the Azure Communication Services network requirements, and call recordings use Azure or Teams storage. Sales Premium features exist only in certain regions and languages (§2.1).

Set up sales basics (the documented checklist): business units → sales teams → sales territories → fiscal period → multiple currencies → product catalog (§1.2); then customize branding, business process flows, forms and views. Territories live under App Settings > Sales Administration > Sales Territories; each has a manager and an optional parent, and one user cannot belong to several territories (create a parent territory that covers them instead).

TaskOrdered steps or rule
Upgrade a license (for example Enterprise to Premium)1) Purchase the new subscription. 2) Assign it to users (Manage product licenses > Replace). 3) Install the app that matches the new license. 4) Delete the previous solution (Advanced Settings > Customization > Solutions). Organization data is preserved.
License expiresThe environment is disabled and its data is deleted after 30 days, unless the tenant still has other related licenses.

Configure mailboxes

Sales tracks email through server-side synchronization (SSS). With Exchange it syncs email, appointments, contacts and tasks; with a POP3/SMTP server only email. A user maps to one mailbox and a mailbox to one user; only mailboxes can be synchronized (not contacts or distribution lists); S/MIME-encrypted messages can't be viewed. Mail syncs about every five minutes and appointments, contacts and tasks every five to twelve minutes, with no SLA.

  1. Power Platform admin center > the environment > Settings > Email > Server profiles. Confirm the default Microsoft Exchange Online profile (created automatically when Exchange Online is in the same tenant) or create one: Email Server Type Exchange Online, authentication Server-to-Server Authentication (Same Tenant) or OAuth (Cross Tenant).
  2. Settings > Email > Email settings: set Server Profile, Incoming Email, Outgoing Email and Appointments, Contacts, and Tasks to server-side synchronization as the default for new users.
  3. Settings > Email > Mailboxes > Active Mailboxes: select existing mailboxes and choose Apply Default Email Settings (you need Read and Write on the Mailbox table).
  4. Choose Approve Email, then Test & Enable Mailbox. Results appear in the Incoming Email Status, Outgoing Email Status and Appointments, Contacts, and Tasks Status columns; failures raise alerts on the mailbox.
Approval ruleDetail
On by defaultProcess emails only for approved users and Process emails only for approved queues (Email settings > Security and permissions). Turn both off to drop the approval requirement.
Who can approveThe Approve Email Addresses for Users or Queues privilege plus System Administrator combined with Global admin, Exchange admin, or the Delegated Mailbox Approver role. Only a Global or Exchange admin can assign Delegated Mailbox Approver, and it can't be assigned to a team.
Self-approvalAllowed when the UPN matches the mailbox email, the mailbox isn't a queue, the user has at least user-level Write on Mailbox, and RequirePrivilegeToSelfApproveEmailAddress is disabled (default) or the user holds the approve privilege.
  • Dynamics 365 App for Outlook needs SSS. Order: set Process Email Using = Server-Side Synchronization → approve, test and enable mailboxes → assign the Dynamics 365 App for Outlook User security role (adding a team to the role doesn't pass privileges to its members) → deploy from Settings > Dynamics 365 App for Outlook to all eligible users or selected users, or let users add it themselves. A mailbox can sync appointments, contacts and tasks with only one organization.
  • Sales Professional app: Sales Settings > Standard settings > Set up email configures Exchange Online automatically. Existing mailboxes are auto-approved only when the primary email equals the UPN and the user has the Sales Professional Person or Sales Professional Manager role; new users need Approve and Test mailboxes.
  • Agent mailbox (Research and engage mode): a shared mailbox, a Dataverse app user with the AIsalesperson role, and SSS set to mail only (Appointment, Contacts and Tasks = None); see §2.2.

Set up and configure business process flows

A business process flow (BPF) shows stages and steps (each step is a column) in a process bar at the top of a form. A required step gates the move to the next stage ("stage-gating"); a required Two Options column must be Yes to pass, so use a Choice column when either answer is acceptable. The system BPFs are Lead to Opportunity Sales Process, Phone to Case Process and Sales Process.

Limit or ruleValue
Active BPFs per table10
Stages per process / steps per stage30 / 30
Tables per process5 (a table relationship you select must be 1:N)
Branch depth5 levels per the branching article; 10 levels per the newer "Create a business process flow" article (Microsoft's articles disagree)
Condition operatorsAND or OR inside one condition, never both. The rule uses steps of the immediately preceding stage; Client API changes don't re-evaluate it.
  1. Power Apps (or Power Automate) > Solutions > your solution > New > Automation > Process > Business process flow; enter Display name, Name and the table. BPFs can't be created or managed from Power Automate outside the solution explorer.
  2. Drag a Stage to a "+" and add Steps (mark Required where needed); drag a Condition between stages to branch; drag a Workflow onto a stage (runs on entry or exit and must use the stage's table) or onto Global Workflow (runs when the process is completed or abandoned).
  3. Validate, Save (a draft can't be used), then Activate.
  4. Use Edit Security Roles to control who can create, read, update or delete instances; System Administrator and System Customizer have access by default.
  • Several BPFs per table are filtered by the user's security role; the process order picks the default, users change it with Switch Process, and several processes can run on one row.
  • A workflow on Stage Exit of the last stage never fires; use a Global Workflow instead.
  • Creating BPFs needs a Power Apps or Power Automate per-user license, or a Dynamics 365 plan with BPF use rights. In Sales Professional use Sales Settings > Customization > Business Process Flows > Create New; afterwards you can't change the entity, system name, owner or category.

Configure the timeline

The timeline control shows activities, notes and posts for a row. Add it in Power Apps > Tables > the table > Forms > the form > Components > Timeline, set the options, then Save and Publish. A form can hold several timelines, and each form (an account has three standard forms) is configured separately.

SettingDefault or rule
Records shown on page10 by default, up to 50, then Load more
Record types to showActivities, Notes and Posts all on; Posts need a Dynamics 365 app
Quick entry record type / sort orderNotes (or Posts) / Descending
Filter pane, search bar, "What you've missed"On by default; Expand filter pane by default and Expand all records by default are off
Activity rollup type (account and contact)Extended, Related or None; None shows only activities directly related to the row
Custom table in the timelineCreate the table with Type = Activity (optionally Enable attachments for notes and files). Activity tables can be owned only by users or teams
PerformanceMore than 10 activity types triggers a warning
Card formsHeader: up to 6 columns, first 2 show; Details: up to 4, first 3 show; Footer isn't shown. A Sort date column you populate overrides the sort
Command actions on activitiesPreview assign, close, delete, open, add to queue (at most five)

Evaluate options for importing and exporting data

NeedUseFacts to remember
One-off load by a seller or adminImport wizard in the app: Import from Excel / CSV / XMLDownload an Excel template and don't edit its columns. Formats .xlsx, .csv, .xml. 8 MB per file, 32 MB for .zip. One file per run. Allow Duplicates choice; alternate key for CSV/XML updates; review mapping and save a data map; Track Progress, then Export Error Rows. Excel import isn't supported for virtual or elastic tables.
Maker import with upsertPower Apps > Tables > Import (Environment Maker role)Primary or alternate keys decide insert vs update. Timezone, multiselect choice, image and file types and system columns such as ownerid and createdon aren't supported. Export > Export data gives a CSV of one table and is cut off after 12 minutes. "New import from Excel" is Preview.
Recurring load from other sourcesDataflows (Power Query)Load into Dataverse (default) or Data Lake Gen2, scheduled refresh, one owner who can edit.
Excel analysisExport to Excel: Excel Online, static worksheet (snapshot), dynamic worksheet (refreshable), PivotTableCalculated, rollup and secured columns can be edited in Excel but can't be imported back; virtual tables aren't supported.
Continuous copy for analyticsAzure Synapse Link for Dataverse or Link to Microsoft Fabric (§2.1)Synapse Link branding is being retired; in Power Apps open Link data.

Import status moves Submitted → Parsing → Transforming → Importing → Completed, and the log shows Success, Failures and Partial Failures. You can delete the source file, the imported records, or both.

Examine the Sales security model

Dataverse security is layered and cumulative: users get the broadest access granted by all their roles and teams.

LayerWhat to know
Security rolesTable privileges: Create, Read, Write, Delete, Append (attach this record to another), Append To (allow other records to attach to it), Assign, Share. Access levels: Organization, Parent: Child Business Unit, Business Unit, User, None; organization-owned tables allow only Organization or None. Roles also carry miscellaneous and privacy-related privileges.
Business unitsOne root business unit; each user belongs to one; each BU gets an automatic default team. Record ownership across business units (Power Platform admin center > environment > Settings > Product > Features) enables the matrix model.
TeamsOwner teams own records and can hold roles; access teams only receive shared records; group teams map to Microsoft Entra security groups.
HierarchyManager hierarchy follows the Manager field and, by default, the same or parent BU. Position hierarchy works across BUs along a position chain and doesn't need a real manager. Direct reports: Read, Write, Append, AppendTo; further down the chain: read-only; depth limits the levels.
Sharing and columnsShare individual records only for exceptions (prefer teams). Column security profiles grant Create, Update or Read on secured columns but never grant record access.
Predefined rolePurpose
System Administrator / System CustomizerFull administration / customization
Vice President of Sales, Sales Manager, SalespersonSales Enterprise and Premium; Sales Manager adds product management, goals and forecasts
Sales Professional Manager / PersonSales Professional app
Forecast Manager, Forecast User, Sequence ManagerFunctional roles (Sequence Manager also needs Basic User or similar)
Sales team member, Sales Professional app access, Sales, Enterprise app accessApp access roles

Assign roles in the sales app under Settings > Advanced Settings > System > Security (Preview) > Users > Manage security roles. Grant Sales Hub access from the Apps page: Sales Hub card > Manage Roles. The AI agent users (D365 Sales LeadQual, AcctRsrch, OutrchAgt) are created automatically and shouldn't be deleted; AISalesPerson is listed among the internal roles and is assigned only to an agent's Dataverse app user (§2.2). Custom roles copied from a predefined role don't inherit later changes to it.

Configure Microsoft 365 functionality, including Microsoft Teams, SharePoint, Outlook, and OneDrive

ServiceHow to enable itRules
Teams chatSales Hub > App Settings > General Settings > Chat and collaborate > Turn on Microsoft Teams chats inside Dynamics 365 for all or selected apps; or Power Platform admin center > environment > Settings > Integration > Teams integration settingsThe setting applies to all customer engagement apps. Chats connect to records (case, account, contact, knowledge article and email by default; add more) with Join chat and Automatically name chats. Dynamics keeps only the record-to-chat mapping. Not available for guests, different tenants or mobile. Only Teams chat sync (Sync Teams chat data with Dynamics 365 records, global administrator required, Teams chat must be enabled first) is Preview.
SharePointEnvironment > Settings > Integration > Document management settings > Enable server-based SharePoint integration > Online > site URL (same tenant) > Finish; then enable document management per tableNeeds SharePoint Online or a Microsoft 365 subscription. Irreversible: you can't return to client-based authentication. Sales Professional: Sales Settings > Connect SharePoint.
OneDrive for BusinessDocument management settings > Enable OneDrive for BusinessDepends on server-based SharePoint integration and at least one active SharePoint site; OneDrive and SharePoint licenses per user; the OneDrive for Business privilege controls access.
OutlookServer-side synchronization plus Dynamics 365 App for Outlook (see Configure mailboxes)Needs the Dynamics 365 App for Outlook User role.

Status notes from the Sales deprecation list: linking Dynamics 365 records to Teams channels is Deprecated (May 2026); "Add to Dynamics 365" from Teams chat messages is Deprecated (January 2026); the Sales Hub Dialer preview was removed (July 2026), so use the Teams dialer.

Exam traps
  • "Enable Dynamics 365 apps" can only be set when the database is created. A wrongly created environment can't be fixed in place; create a new one.
  • Server-based SharePoint integration is one-way, and OneDrive for Business can't be enabled without it.
  • Mailbox approval is on by default. Delegated Mailbox Approver still needs System Administrator, only a Global or Exchange admin can assign it, and it can't go to a team.
  • BPF limits: 5 tables per process, 10 active BPFs per table, 30 stages; a condition can use AND or OR but not both, and only steps from the preceding stage.
  • Import limits are 8 MB per file but 32 MB for .zip; the maker Export data command produces CSV, not Excel; Append and Append To are different privileges on different tables.
  • Position hierarchy (cross-BU, no real manager needed) is not manager hierarchy (Manager field, same or parent BU by default).

sections.title: 1.2 Create and manage the product catalog
sections.html:
Skills measured: Configure products and product families • Create and manage price lists, including currencies. Practice by building a tiny catalog in a Sales Hub environment: one discount list, one unit group, a family with a product and a bundle, a USD price list and a second currency with its own price list.

Configure products and product families

Units, discounts and prices depend on each other, so the documentation says to create the catalog components in a fixed order:

  1. Create discount lists (price breaks by quantity).
  2. Create a unit group and add its units.
  3. Create the products, families or bundles; each product links to a unit group and a default unit.
  4. Create the price lists.
  5. Add each product to one or more price lists as price list items (from the product form or the price list form).
  6. Select a default price list on the product. The pricing engine uses it when the price list on the opportunity, quote or order has no price for that product.
TopicWhat to know
WhereSales Hub > Change area > App Settings > Product Catalog > Families and Products (Add Family, Add Product, Add Bundle). Product families exist only in the Sales Hub app; in Sales Professional, products and price lists are managed from the site map.
WhoSystem Administrator, System Customizer, Sales Manager, Vice President of Sales, Vice President of Marketing or CEO-Business Manager. A role needs Create on the Product table; products are always created at organization level, even if the role is set to user level.
FamiliesAs many levels as you want (a family inside a family). Children inherit the family's properties; override a property on the child. The family used when you create an item becomes its parent.
Product fieldsName, Product ID, Parent, Valid From/To (no logic except that To must be later than From), Unit Group, Default Unit, Default Price List (read-only until the first save), Decimals Supported (whole number 0 to 5), Subject.
StateHow you get thereRules
DraftDefault for a new record (unless Create product in active state is on, which covers only products without a parent family)Not available to sellers
ActivePublish (or Publish Hierarchy on a family)A child can be published only if its parent family is active; you can't publish several records at once except through Publish Hierarchy. Sellers can choose only published items
Under RevisionRevise an active record; revising a family puts all its children under revisionPublish again, or Revert to the last active version
RetiredRetireRetired families can't be reactivated; only a standalone product can be activated again (unparent a product first if you may need it back)
  • Bundles sell several products as one unit. A bundle can't contain families, kits or other bundles, can mark products optional, and (with an optional product) can be added only to a price list that contains that product in the same unit.
  • Add or delete bundle products only while the bundle is Draft or Retired. For an Active or Under Revision bundle, clone it: the clone gets a new ID in Draft state.
Product Catalog Settings (App Settings > Product Catalog)Effect
Enhanced experience for adding productsSearch-and-compare Add products dialog (not on mobile)
Create product in active stateSkips Draft, only for products without a parent family
Allow selection of default pricelistUses territory default price lists on opportunities
System pricing calculationOn = system pricing engine; off = custom pricing
Make price list optionalSellers can add products without a price list
Max products in a bundle / max propertiesDefaults 15 / 50 (properties limit applies when you publish)
Discount calculation methodLine item (default) or Per unit. With a price of 100, quantity 11 and discount 10: line item = (100 × 11) − 10 = 1,090; per unit = (100 − 10) × 11 = 990

Create and manage price lists, including currencies

A price list tells sellers what to charge. Create it under App Settings > Product Catalog > Price Lists with a Name, Start/End Date and Currency. You need at least one price list for each currency you trade in, and the Price List table inherits its privileges from the Product table. Each price list item holds a Product, Unit, the list's Currency, an optional Discount List and a Quantity Selling Option (whole, partial or both).

Pricing methodPrice is...
Currency AmountA fixed amount you type (ignores the product list price)
Percent of ListA percentage of the product's list price
Percent Markup - Current Cost / Standard CostCost plus a percentage markup
Percent Margin - Current Cost / Standard CostPriced to yield a percentage margin on cost
  • Rounding applies only when the method isn't Currency Amount: Rounding Policy None, Up, Down or To Nearest; Rounding Option Ends in or Multiple of; plus a Rounding Amount. For prices that always end in 0.99, round Up with the option Ends in and amount 0.99.
  • Give a price list a default for a territory on its Territory Relationship tab (Add New Connection); this works together with Allow selection of default pricelist.
Currency taskWhere and rules
Add or edit a currencyPower Platform admin center > environment > Settings > Business > Currencies > New (System Administrator). Currency Type System or Custom; Currency Code (a custom code is three letters); Currency Precision 0 to 4; name; symbol; Currency Conversion (exchange rate to the base currency, kept up to date by you).
Remove a currencyA currency used by records can't be deleted, only deactivated; existing records keep it, new transactions can't select it.
Base currencyChosen when the environment is created. It can be changed later with the Marketplace Base Currency Conversion app: back up, install, create the single BaseCurrencyConversion record with the new base, correct exchange rates, add historical CurrencyExchangeRate rows for the whole data date range, then Start Conversion and watch Conversion Status.
Decimal precision levelScope
Pricing decimal precisionOrganization setting, 0 to 4 (Advanced Settings > System > Administration > General). Covers product list price, standard and current cost, price list item amount and rounding amount, and price per unit on opportunity, quote, order and invoice products
Currency precisionPer currency record, 0 to 4; applies to the other currency columns
Field-level precisionColumn setting (Precision source = Precision property), 0 to 4

Product Decimals Supported (0 to 5) is separate: it validates the quantity on a line when the product has no associated price list. On orders and invoices, Prices Locked plus the line's Pricing choice (Use Default or Override Price) decide whether Price Per Unit can be edited or follows later price list changes.

Exam traps
  • The catalog order is discount lists, unit groups, products, price lists, price list items, then default price list; candidates often put price lists before products.
  • You can't add a product to an Active or Under Revision bundle. Clone it (new ID, Draft); Revise doesn't unlock the bundle's product list.
  • Retired product families can't be reactivated, and Publish fails for a child while its parent family isn't active.
  • A price list is tied to one currency; selling in a second currency needs a second price list. A used currency can only be deactivated.
  • Pricing decimal precision (0-4) is not Decimals Supported on the product (0-5). The base currency, although chosen at environment creation, can be changed later with the Base Currency Conversion app.
  • Product families belong to the Sales Hub app only.

sections.title: 2.1 Design an AI-first sales strategy
sections.html:
Skills measured: Augment seller workflows by using Copilot and agents • Design the sales data model in Dataverse • Evaluate options for reporting and visualization • Differentiate features in Sales plans. Practice by comparing the Copilot in Dynamics 365 Sales pane with the Sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, drawing the lead-to-invoice tables and relationships, and building one Power BI report on Dataverse.

Augment seller workflows by using Copilot and agents

Copilot in Dynamics 365 SalesSales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot
Where it worksBuilt into the Dynamics 365 Sales appTeams, Outlook, Word, Excel and Dynamics 365 Sales
Chat historyNone across sessionsKept across sessions and apps
MenuCopilot > App SkillsCopilot > Chat
CRM supportDynamics 365 Sales onlyDynamics 365 Sales and Salesforce
Typical useSummaries of leads, opportunities and accounts; recent changes; meeting prep; SharePoint answers; email assist; account newsCRM-grounded email drafts, meeting takeaways, CRM field updates in the flow of work
  • The documentation calls the Sales agent the evolution of the Copilot experience and says it will become the preferred way to reach Copilot in Dynamics 365 Sales. Migration is immediate when you have no customization (glossary and synonyms are shared); redo summary-field configuration in the Sales agent setup, rebuild custom topics and skills as declarative agents, and note that welcome-card and prompt-suggestion customization isn't supported.
  • Copilot in Sales returns only data the signed-in user can access. Turn it on under Sales Hub > App Settings > General Settings > Copilot; Turn audit on there so "recent changes" works. Four control levels apply: tenant control for model-driven chat, tenant control for Copilot in Sales (Power Platform admin center > Copilot > Settings > Dynamics 365 Sales), Microsoft Entra groups, and the app-level setting.
  • Licensing: Sales Enterprise, Premium and Relationship Sales include the basic Sales agent features (email replies, conversation intelligence in Teams); the premium features need a Microsoft 365 Copilot license. Install needs a Microsoft 365 admin role; customizing needs System Administrator or System Customizer; sellers need Salesperson or Sales Manager. The Sales agent isn't supported in GCC, DoD or Dynamics 365 on-premises. Set it up from Sales Hub: App Settings > General Settings > Copilot > Sales agent > Setup.
Agent or capabilityJobStatus and notes
Sales Qualification Agent (§3.2)Researches leads, checks fit with the target customer profile, drafts or sends outreach, hands over promising leadsTwo modes: Research-only (research, fit, draft email) and Research and engage (adds BANT, sending, intent detection, follow-ups). One mode per org; Research-only can be upgraded, not reverted
Sales Opportunity Agent (§4.1)Combines CRM, email, meetings and web research; flags risks; prioritizes deals; formerly Opportunity Research AgentSeveral instances per product line or segment. No preview banner on its overview, although the common-prerequisites page still tags it (preview)
Sales Close Agent (§4.2)End-to-end engagement for high-velocity, low-complexity deals (accounts, contacts, leads, opportunities)Preview (production-ready). The docs say new instances can't be created from September 30, 2026 and existing instances are removed on October 30, 2026; the named replacement is the Sales Development agent (Preview, Teams-based, Microsoft Agent 365)
Sales Research Agent (§4.3)Natural-language "research canvas" over Sales data, Fabric Lakehouse, other Dataverse and CSV/Excel/PDF filesIts FAQ is labeled (preview)
Recommended Actions AgentOne prioritized action list across agentsActions from the Sales Opportunity and Sales Qualification agents and custom agents are charged; Data Enrichment actions are shown but not charged
AI-powered Data EnrichmentEnriches opportunity data from email interactionsListed in the agent overview
Seller needUse
Summaries and meeting prep inside Sales HubCopilot in Dynamics 365 Sales
Insights and drafts inside Outlook or Teams, or Salesforce usersSales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot
Qualify a high volume of inbound leadsSales Qualification Agent (Research and engage if the agent must email and follow up)
Spot deal risk and prioritize open dealsSales Opportunity Agent with Recommended Actions
Ask pipeline questions in natural languageSales Research Agent

Dynamics 365 Sales also exposes a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server so other agents can use Sales tools. Deprecated Copilot items: document summary, the full-screen Copilot view, the "emails that need follow up" prompt, and Copilot email in the side pane.

Design the sales data model in Dataverse

The sales process maps to a table chain: Lead (Qualify) → Opportunity (Develop) → Quote (Propose) → Order (Close) → Invoice (Fulfill), with Account, Contact, Product and Price List around it. Qualifying a lead creates or links account, contact and opportunity rows according to the lead qualification settings.

Design questionAnswer
Table typeStandard; Activity (time-based, owned only by users or teams, primary column Subject); Virtual (external data); Elastic (very large datasets). Ownership (organization vs user/team) is chosen at creation and can't change.
Relationship typesOnly 1:N and N:N (N:1 is the child view of 1:N). A lookup column creates a 1:N; N:N uses an intersect table (opportunity and competitor). Use connections for informal links. Anyone who can read a row sees the lookup's primary name, so keep secrets out of it.
BehaviorsActions Assign, Reparent, Share, Unshare, Merge, Delete, Rollup View; settings Cascade All, Cascade Active, Cascade User-Owned, Cascade None, Remove Link, Restrict. A parental relationship cascades Assign, Reparent, Share and Delete; usually one per table pair. A custom table can't be the primary table in a cascading relationship with a system table.
Column mappingCopies defaults when a related row is created in context (Account to Contact). It is a snapshot, not a sync; both columns need the same type and format; the target must be at least as long; edit it in classic solution explorer and publish; Generate Mappings replaces existing mappings.
Lead qualificationSales Hub > App Settings > General Settings > Lead + Opportunity management > Lead Qualification: per record type choose Seller or Automatic creation; duplicate detection applies; sellers can create up to 5 opportunities from one qualified lead; optional Copilot lead summary. Legacy option: System Settings, Sales tab.
Pricing rowsAn opportunity product inherits its owning business unit from the parent opportunity (you can't set it on the line); price list items tie product, unit and currency.
Agent tablesCustom roles need read on msdyn_salesagentrun, msdyn_salesagentprofile, msdyn_salesagenthandover, msdyn_engagereadinessagentresult and msdyn_synthesizeroutput to use the AI hub; Sales Qualification Agent results land in msdyn_leadagentresult and msdyn_accountresearchresult.

Evaluate options for reporting and visualization

OptionUse whenKey facts
Interactive experience dashboardsReal-time, role-based work queues in the appMulti-stream (many streams, each on one table) and single-stream (one table); interactive charts act as visual filters; solution-aware, but queues aren't.
Power BI embedded in the appExisting Power BI reports in the sales appEnable the Power BI visualization embedding setting; Solutions > New > Dashboard > Power BI Embedded; add it to the app as a dashboard page.
Power BI Desktop + Dataverse connectorCustom BI on DataverseRequires Enable TDS endpoint; Import (recommended, cached, scheduled) vs DirectQuery (real time, stricter Dataverse security); TCP 1433 and/or 5558; the Legacy connector handles results over 80 MB.
Link to Microsoft FabricLakehouse analytics without ETLPower Apps Link data > New link > Fabric link; creates a Lakehouse, SQL endpoint and Power BI dataset; consumes Dataverse storage. Azure Synapse Link exports to your own Synapse or Data Lake Gen2; its branding is being retired.
SSRS fetch-based reportsPaginated reports inside the model-driven appAdd the Report table to the app; Report Wizard or Report Authoring Extension; not available in canvas apps or on mobile.
ExcelAd hoc analysisExcel templates (Power Platform admin center > Settings > Templates > Document templates; at most 50 records when created from a view; environment-bound) and export to a dynamic worksheet or PivotTable.
Sales Research AgentNatural-language pipeline questionsResearch canvas with visualizations (§4.3).

Deprecated Sales usage reports (effective December 1, 2025; a sample Power BI report is offered unsupported) and the Sales Analytics and Process Analytics Power BI template apps (May 2025).

Differentiate features in Sales plans

PlanWhat it adds
Sales ProfessionalStreamlined app for small and medium businesses; a subset of the Enterprise tables; its own app and roles; product families are not available (Sales Hub only)
Sales EnterpriseLead-to-cash automation, forecasting, in-app marketing campaigns; Premium features such as sales accelerator and predictive scoring with limited monthly capacity
Sales PremiumEverything in Enterprise plus guided selling (sales accelerator), relationship intelligence (assistant, who knows whom, conversation intelligence, relationship analytics) and predictive models (lead and opportunity scoring, predictive forecasting), with no capacity limit
Microsoft Relationship SalesSales Enterprise plus LinkedIn Sales Navigator; bought only through a Microsoft representative or partner
Team MemberSales Team Member app: view contacts, accounts, leads and opportunities, add notes and activities
Capacity (Sales Hub > App Settings > Overview > Quick setup)Sales EnterpriseSales Premium
Sales accelerator1,500 sequence-connected records per monthNo limit
Predictive lead and opportunity scoring1,500 records per monthNo limit
Relationship intelligenceBasic insights and who-knows-whom from Dynamics 365 dataAdvanced insights and who-knows-whom from Dynamics 365 and Exchange data
  • Sales Premium is offered only in listed regions, and feature availability varies by region (for example, premium forecasting isn't available in GCC or France). Premium forecasting also needs a qualifying license and more than 10 closed opportunities with actual and estimated values and dates.
  • Copilot Studio credits can be included with eligible Dynamics 365 Premium licenses; the amounts and terms are in the Dynamics 365 Licensing Guide (§2.2), so confirm them there rather than relying on a figure from memory.
  • To change plans use the upgrade steps in §1.1.
Exam traps
  • Copilot in Dynamics 365 Sales is not the Sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot: only the Sales agent keeps chat history, works in Outlook and Teams, and supports Salesforce.
  • Research-only mode never sends email; sending, BANT and follow-ups belong to Research and engage.
  • Sales Close Agent is a Preview feature that is being retired, and it is a different product from the Sales Opportunity Agent.
  • Enterprise already includes some Premium features, but the sales accelerator and predictive lead and opportunity scoring are capped (1,500 records per month); Premium removes the cap and adds Exchange-based relationship insights.
  • Relationship Sales can't be bought directly, and product families need Sales Hub, not Sales Professional.
  • Dataverse allows only 1:N and N:N relationships; table ownership can't be changed after creation; a Power BI Dataverse connector report needs the TDS endpoint turned on.

sections.title: 2.2 Prepare to deploy agents
sections.html:
Skills measured: Configure prerequisites for deploying agents • Configure capacity, billing, and credits. Practice by walking the Prerequisites page in the Dynamics 365 AI hub, registering an app and an app user for an agent, and linking a Sales environment to prepaid capacity and to a pay-as-you-go billing plan.

Configure prerequisites for deploying agents

The built-in sales agents share a one-time set of common prerequisites. Until every one is marked Done, the Create option on the AI agents page stays disabled. Each agent then adds its own requirements, which its own setup article covers.

  1. Sign in with the Power Platform administrator role.
  2. In Sales Hub choose Change area > App Settings > General Settings > Dynamics 365 AI hub, then under Agent manager select Create and manage agents. The Prerequisites page appears the first time you create an agent.
  3. Complete the three items: Microsoft Copilot Studio capacity (Set up opens the Power Platform admin center), Move data across regions (Accept terms), and AI prompts (Set up; lets the agent use custom or predefined prompts).
  4. Select Refresh and confirm each item shows Done.
  5. In the Power Platform admin center turn on AI insight cards (notify sellers about insights on the opportunity record) and AI Agents (enables configuring and using AI agents in Sales).
  6. Select Create.
SettingWhere and rules
AI Agents / Copilot togglesPower Platform admin center > Copilot > Settings > Dynamics 365 Sales; choose an environment or environment group > Edit setting > On > Save. On by default; changed by a tenant admin.
Move data across regionsEnvironment > Generative AI features card > Edit. The same pane has Bing search and Microsoft 365 services. A Power Platform or Dynamics 365 admin gives consent. The checkbox isn't shown for U.S. or government cloud environments; when shown, Bing search needs it ticked; data already moved can't be pulled back.
AI promptsEnvironment > Settings > Product > Features > AI Builder > AI prompts (on by default); an environment group rule can lock it.
Agent-specific requirementResearch-onlyResearch and engageNotes
Azure (Microsoft Entra) app registrationYesYesNeeds the Entra Application Developer role; copy the Application (client) ID
Dataverse app user with role AIsalespersonYesYesSystem Administrator; Power Platform admin center > Settings > Users + permissions > Application users > New app user; root business unit
Shared mailbox–YesGlobal, Exchange or Exchange Recipient admin; Exchange admin center > Recipients > Mailboxes
Server-side synchronization for that mailbox–YesReplace the app user's email with the shared mailbox, Approve Email, set Appointment, Contacts and Tasks = None, Test & Enable Mailbox
  • The table follows the requirements article. The Sales Qualification Agent setup page adds that without server-side synchronization the agent doesn't generate outreach emails or engage with leads.
  • Also required for the Sales Qualification Agent: admin permissions in Sales, a Copilot Studio license, the modern UI for Sales Hub, in-app notifications, and data policies (DLP) that allow the connectors Knowledge source with public websites and data, Microsoft Copilot Studio, Microsoft Dataverse and Direct Line channels in Copilot Studio (plus the SharePoint/OneDrive and documents knowledge sources when internal documents are used).
  • Sales Opportunity Agent (§4.1): the common prerequisites, a Copilot Studio license, modern UI, the same connectors without Microsoft Dataverse, plus Bing search (Accept terms), Dataverse Search (turn on search indexing for Dataverse intelligence and the global search bar), and optionally Microsoft 365 Services so it can read seller email in place; server-side synchronization is the alternative, and email tracking must be allowed in each seller's personalization settings.
  • Sales Close Agent (§4.2): the same four requirements as Research and engage. Status: Preview (production-ready) and being retired, with new instances blocked from September 30, 2026 and existing ones removed on October 30, 2026; the named replacement is the Sales Development agent (Preview), which needs Microsoft 365 Copilot and Teams licenses, Copilot Frontier, and the Agent 365 public preview enabled by a Global Administrator.
  • Rules: only one Sales Qualification Agent mode per organization; Research-only can be upgraded to Research and engage but not back; stopping the agent only stops new leads; a configured agent can't be deleted (contact Microsoft support). Agent users (D365 Sales LeadQual, AcctRsrch, OutrchAgt) are created automatically.
  • AI hub access: custom roles need read on msdyn_salesagentrun, msdyn_salesagentprofile, msdyn_salesagenthandover, msdyn_engagereadinessagentresult and msdyn_synthesizeroutput; the out-of-the-box Salesperson and Sales Manager roles need nothing extra to work handed-over leads. Test agents in a sandbox and move them to production by importing the agent solution.

Configure capacity, billing, and credits

Copilot Studio's billing unit is the Copilot Credit. Starting September 1, 2025 it replaced "messages"; the quantity per prepaid pack and the pay-as-you-go rate didn't change, and some Sales pages still say "messages". Sales Copilot and agent capabilities use consumption-based billing with two models, and both need the Sales environment linked to a Power Platform environment.

Prepaid capacityPay-as-you-go
What you buyCopilot Studio capacity pack subscription, in advanceNothing up front; billed monthly to an Azure subscription for credits actually used
Setup1) Buy the pack in the Microsoft 365 admin center (customer) or Partner Center (reseller). 2) Assign the capacity to the Power Platform environment in the Power Platform admin center. 3) Link the Sales environment.1) Have an active Azure subscription and create a billing plan: admin center Licensing > Pay-as-you-go plans > New billing plan (subscription, resource group, Power Platform product, environments). 2) Link the Sales environment.
RulesCredits are pooled across the tenant and must be assigned to an environment; unused credits don't carry over to the next monthAvailable for production and sandbox environments; an environment links to one billing plan; billing policies can be created by an environment admin, Power Platform admin, Global admin or Dynamics 365 admin
  • You can use both on the same Sales environment; prepaid capacity is consumed first.
  • Monitor and allocate: Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Summary (Prepaid capacity and Pay-as-you-go credits cards, Environments tab, downloadable reports by environment, agent or user); Manage Capacity assigns credits to an environment. Capacity overages: Draw from the available capacity in my tenant or Bill to my pay-as-you-go billing plan. Manage Agents sets a monthly limit per agent with notifications and an optional hard stop (limits aren't instant).
  • In the Sales app: Sales checks the quota and sends in-app notifications when it is low or depleted. When it is depleted the AI capability is unavailable until capacity is added: reallocate or buy more for prepaid, adjust budgets in Azure Cost Management for pay-as-you-go. Allocating credits to the Sales environment is the only way to stop other agents in the tenant using that capacity.
  • What consumes capacity: the Sales Qualification Agent uses it for research, target-customer-profile matching and the first outreach email (viewing existing insights is free); the Sales Opportunity Agent processes every open in-scope opportunity on its first run, then scales with in-scope opportunities and refresh frequency (narrow scope and refresh to save credits); Recommended Actions charges per prioritized action, but not for Data Enrichment actions.
  • Bundled credits: specific Dynamics 365 licenses include monthly credits per user (not cumulative, reset monthly); the Licensing Guide lists the amounts.
Copilot Studio rate (standard harness)Credits
Classic answer1
Generative answer2
Agent action5
Tenant graph grounding10
Agent flow actions, per 100 actions13

Enforcement: when a tenant on the prepaid model reaches 125% of its capacity, custom agents are disabled (a conversation in progress isn't interrupted; the admin gets an email and a notice in the admin center). Agent flows are blocked when credits run out, while the agent keeps answering. Pay-as-you-go and overage billing avoid the stop.

Exam traps
  • The common prerequisites (capacity, data movement, AI prompts) are not the agent-specific ones (Azure app, app user, shared mailbox, server-side sync). Both sets must be finished; Create stays disabled until the common ones are Done.
  • Shared mailbox and server-side sync are the Research and engage additions; the app registration and AIsalesperson app user apply to both modes.
  • The Move data across regions checkbox is hidden for U.S. and government cloud environments, and Bing search can't be ticked without it when it is shown.
  • The agent can't be deleted once configured, and the mode can only move from Research-only to Research and engage.
  • Prepaid and pay-as-you-go can coexist; prepaid is consumed first. Pay-as-you-go needs an Azure subscription and a billing plan, and works only for production and sandbox environments.
  • "Messages" in older Sales pages and Copilot Credits are the same billing unit after September 1, 2025; credits must be assigned to the environment that runs the agent.

sections.title: 2.3 Configure AI-powered intelligence and insights features
sections.html:
Skills measured: Configure the Sales accelerator • Configure work assignment and distribution • Set up conversational intelligence • Configure predictive scoring • Set up relationship intelligence • Configure Copilot features, including record summarization • Configure and use forecasts to help improve sales performance • Set up goals and goal metrics. Build each item once in a trial or sandbox Sales Hub environment: a sequence, a segment with an assignment rule, a recording policy, a lead scoring model, a forecast and a goal with a rollup query.

Configure the Sales accelerator

The sales accelerator is an engagement workspace: a prioritised work list for sellers plus sequences (conditional workflows of activities) that managers connect to records. Out of the box it is available in Sales Hub with limited functionality (work items created through the timeline for contact, opportunity, lead and account records). Sequences and segments need the workspace to be configured and a suitable licence. It is not supported on mobile devices.

First-run setup (ordered):

  1. In Sales Hub select Change area → Sales Insights settings.
  2. Under Sales accelerator select Workspace → Quick setup.
  3. Add the security roles that may use the accelerator.
  4. Optional: Add sample data (sandbox and trial environments only).
  5. In Record type and form choose the record types and the form that receives the Up next widget. Leads, opportunities, accounts and contacts are preselected; organization-owned tables are not supported.
  6. Select Update.
NeedWhere to configure it
Change roles or record types laterWorkspace → Manage access and record type → Configure → Publish. Changes can take up to 12 hours to show (refreshing the browser twice shows them sooner).
Filters and sorts in the work listWorkspace → Customize workspace → Filtering and sorting. Filters are basic (one field) or advanced (several fields combined with AND); ungrouped filters land in More filters; the out-of-the-box Default filters can't be edited, moved or deleted. Default sorts: activity type, due date, name, record type, score, sequence name.
Seller-level behaviourSequences → Settings: Seller availability (with Wait time computation to skip non-working days), Sequence activities (Create linked activities, optional Lock settings), Sequence reporting, Phone number priority (Default, Fallback1, Fallback2; needs a channel provider and Teams calling).
Custom table in the work listEnable Activities, Connections, Sending email on the table, add it under Record type and form, and add the Up next widget to its form (it is on the Default Main and Sales Insight forms by default).

Sequences. Sales Insights settings → Sales accelerator → Sequences → New sequence → Use template or Use blank sequence → name, description and Entity (default Lead) → designer. The first step is Sequence start here. Deactivate a sequence before assigning it; an organization can have up to 250 active sequences.

Step groupWhat it contains
StepsA/B test, email, automated email, text message, automated text message, phone call, task, Set wait time
ConditionsYes/No branches on an email (open, reply, link opened, attachment downloaded), phone call, field value or business process stage. They work as designed only when the Power Automate flow Sales Insights Adaptive sequence timeout flow is turned on; email conditions also need email engagement and sequence activities enabled.
CommandsAdvance to another sequence (can't be the first step; nothing can follow it) and Update field (two-option and option-set fields)
LinkedInLinkedIn social-selling activities

Sales Enterprise quick setup: on the Sales settings page (App Settings) choose Sales accelerator → Quick setup. The licence includes 1,500 sequence-connected records per month; admins can monitor usage, a warning symbol appears when it is exceeded, and a licence upgrade is needed to continue without interruption. Predictive scores (see Configure predictive scoring below) appear in the work list when scoring is configured.

Deprecated Setting seller availability through the Outlook calendar is no longer possible; use the Dynamics 365 calendar. Playbooks were replaced by sequences.

Exam traps
  • Organization-owned tables cannot be added as record types; a custom user-owned table also needs Activities, Connections and Sending email enabled.
  • Workspace settings (record types, filters, sorts) and sequence settings (availability, linked activities, reporting, phone priority) are on different pages under the same Sales accelerator heading.
  • Published workspace changes can take up to 12 hours; refreshing twice is the documented shortcut.
  • A condition step that never branches usually means the Adaptive sequence timeout flow is off.
  • 1,500 is the Enterprise quick-setup cap on sequence-connected records per month; 250 is the cap on active sequences.

Configure work assignment and distribution

Work assignment (Sales Insights settings → Sales accelerator → Work assignment) automates ownership of leads, opportunities and seller insights. It has three parts: segments (group records by conditions), sequences (the activity steps, connected to segments) and assignment rules (route matching records to sellers, teams or queues). The sales accelerator must already be configured.

Recommended configuration order:

  1. Select the security roles that rules can assign to (Settings → Eligible security roles → Manage: all roles or specific roles).
  2. Create and activate segments.
  3. Create sequences.
  4. Connect segments to sequences.
  5. Set seller attributes and maximum capacity.
  6. Set seller availability and calendar.
  7. Create and activate assignment rules.
Rule sectionWhat you choose
2. Eligible recordsA segment (default: all records), up to 10 conditions, optionally Consider records created in the last N hours; if no seller takes the record in that time it is marked overdue
3. Assign toAny seller, Sellers with matching attributes, Specific sellers, Teams with matching attributes, Specific teams, Queues with matching attributes, Specific queue (up to 5 conditions for matching options)
4. Distribute byRound robin or Load balancing; only for seller assignments (team and queue members pick records up themselves). Options: Assign if seller is available within N hours and Assign leads based on seller capacity
MethodPrimary considerationUse when
Round robinWho was assigned a record longest ago (order is stored at organization level, not per rule; manual and add-in assignments count)Fair turn-taking regardless of workload
Load balancingSeller capacity, i.e. how many active records they holdSellers have uneven workloads and everyone should stay equally busy
  • Capacity: available capacity = maximum capacity − consumed capacity. Consumed capacity counts only the active records of the entity types that have assignment rules (max 50, 20 leads plus 10 opportunities, rules only for leads → 30 available). The capacity option skips sellers with 0 or less and leaves the record unassigned if nobody qualifies.
  • Availability: N is 1–120 hours, evaluated in six 24-hour buckets; if the first bucket is empty, round robin supersedes load balancing. Sellers who set no hours count as always available.
  • Evaluation: a rule considers only records created or updated after activation; rules run top to bottom and the first match wins (default order is creation order, newest last).
  • Limits: 250 active segments; a segment can have many rules but only 10 active; a segment has up to 10 conditions; only active records can join a segment.
  • Seller attributes: Settings → Seller attributes → Manage; values come from Pull from a data field or Create manually and the source can't be changed later. Capacity is set per seller or for a group (Set capacity).
  • Availability sources: Work assignment settings → Set availability (one seller at a time), the calendar API on msdyn_extendedusersetting, or a seller attribute such as On vacation. Turn off Assign records for a seller who is away.
  • Monitor: Monitor tab shows To be processed (assigned within about two minutes) and Processed; Needs attention means segmentation, assignment or sequence connection failed — open View status details.
Exam traps
  • Segments choose which records and connect them to sequences; assignment rules choose who owns them; sequences define the steps.
  • Round robin order is organization-wide, so one rule can give a seller two records in a row; load balancing can still fall back to round-robin criteria.
  • Capacity only counts entity types that have rules; opportunities owned by a seller don't reduce lead capacity when only lead rules exist.
  • The record-age timeout (created in the last N hours) is different from the seller-availability window (1–120 hours).
  • Edit rules and segments in the expression builder, not in Dataverse; conditions can be moved between a segment and a rule to stay inside the limits.

Set up conversational intelligence

The docs call it conversation intelligence. It analyses call recordings from Teams (or third-party dialers) together with Sales data to give managers KPIs, transcripts, sentiment, tracked keywords and coaching insight. Admin settings: Sales Insights settings → Productivity → Conversation intelligence. Teams prerequisites: Teams Phone System with a licence, a Teams licence and the Teams dialer enabled (§5.1). Call data and transcripts are processed with Azure OpenAI Service; if the region lacks it, the nearest region that has it is used.

  1. Create a recording policy (Call providers and recording → choose Teams → name, recording option, security roles). The roles need read on the Recording table. Several policies can target different roles.
  2. Choose call recording storage and retention.
  3. Under Business settings add keywords and competitors (at least one of each is required to enable the feature) and keep Enable call summary selected.
  4. Optional: data-consent read-only access and preview features; then Publish and accept the terms.
Recording optionBehaviour
Manually record all participantsSeller starts recording; everyone recorded
Manually record all participants, sellers are automatically recordedSeller auto-recorded; seller starts or stops customer recording
Automatically record all participantsEveryone recorded automatically
Automatically record all participants, sellers can stop recordingAutomatic, seller may stop it
Storage optionNotes
Microsoft provided storageDefault; retention 30 or 90 days
Your own Azure storageThe docs say to choose it to keep data longer than 90 days; enter the storage name and container name you created in Azure
Microsoft Dataverse storageOrg-level, no Azure account; purge with recurring Bulk Record Deletion jobs in the Power Platform admin center (Created On older than N days), one job per parent table: Conversation Aggregated Insights, SCI Conversation, Recording, Transcript
  • Managers (Personal settings → Productivity → Conversation intelligence → Get started) can add team-only keywords and competitors, shorten the language list and pick top performers manually or automatically by won opportunities or lead qualification. Their settings don't change the admin's.
  • Sales Enterprise quick setup: Sales settings → Conversation intelligence → Quick setup: turn on Teams calls and Recording with real-time transcription and insights; the licence includes unlimited conversation-intelligence hours and Teams calling hours.
  • Languages: transcription is native for 19 language variants; non-native insights are generated after translating to English. The full insight set is native only for English (US and UK).
  • Preview Hide credit card info in transcripts and call categorization for short calls. Removed The Sales Hub Dialer (preview) was removed; use the Teams dialer.
Exam traps
  • Conversation intelligence can't be enabled without at least one keyword and one competitor.
  • The retention setting offers only 30 or 90 days for Microsoft-provided storage; longer needs your own storage or Dataverse with deletion jobs.
  • Dataverse retention is not set in the conversation intelligence settings; it is a Power Platform admin task.
  • Admin settings sit under Sales Insights settings; manager settings under Personal settings.
  • The feature is for coaching, not for employment decisions; recording notice and consent are the customer's responsibility.

Configure predictive scoring

Predictive lead scoring and opportunity scoring train a model on closed history and score open records. Scores appear in views (for example My Open Leads Scored) and in a widget on the form. Both write to the Predictive Score (msdyn_predictivescore) table. They belong to the premium Sales Insights features, so those must be enabled first.

ItemLead scoringOpportunity scoring
Outcome usedQualified vs disqualifiedWon vs lost
Minimum history40 qualified + 40 disqualified leads created and closed inside the training period40 won + 40 lost; a per-stage model also needs 40 closed in the last stage
Training period3 months to 2 years (default 2 years); data syncs to the data lake in about 4 hours; leads or opportunities that abandoned the chosen business process flow are ignored
ModelsUp to 10 per type (published and unpublished); a warning appears if a new model would score the same records
  1. Change area → Sales Insights settings → Predictive models → Lead scoring (or Opportunity scoring).
  2. Review the defaults — name (letters, digits, underscore; no spaces), business process flow, state option set and qualified/disqualified values, filter column and values, Train with leads from the past — then Get started (disabled if there is too little history).
  3. Wait for training, check Model performance: Ready to publish, OK to publish or Not ready to publish (based on the AUC range; you may still publish).
  4. Select Publish. Retrain automatically (every 15 days) is on by default after publishing.
  • Grades: A, B, C, D (green, purple, yellow, red); admins set the score ranges and changing one boundary moves the neighbouring grade. Sellers also see score trend (Improving, Declining, Steady, Not enough info) and the top positive and negative reasons.
  • Real-time scoring: new leads are scored within minutes; updated leads re-score about every 24 hours.
  • Sales Enterprise quick setup: Sales settings → Lead + opportunity scoring → Quick setup → Create and publish; 1,500 scored records per month; widgets are added to the Sales Insights form only (add them to custom forms yourself).
Exam traps
  • 40 and 40 are both required: a surplus of one outcome doesn't help.
  • Grades A–D belong to scoring; relationship health uses Good/Fair/Poor and the agent's rating uses Hot/Warm/Cold.
  • Per-stage modelling exists only for opportunity scoring and can be enabled only when adding a model.
  • The model can be published even when it is Not ready to publish, but it will perform poorly.

Set up relationship intelligence

Relationship intelligence combines relationship analytics and health (KPIs, health score) and who knows whom (colleagues who can introduce you to a lead or contact). Know the two tiers:

BasicEnhanced
SetupNone; out of the box in all regions for Sales Hub usersAdmin enables relationship intelligence; needs a specific licence
Data usedEmails, appointments and calls in Dynamics 365Dynamics 365 plus Exchange emails and meetings when server-side synchronization is enabled
KPI refreshNear real timeEvery 24 hours
Who knows whomUp to five colleagues, ranked by frequencyFrequency and recency; first results within a day of consent, complete after about four days
  1. Prerequisites: premium Sales Insights features enabled; for Exchange data enable server-side synchronization for Exchange and have sellers set Track in Personalization settings → Emails; Office 365 data must sit in an allowed geography (EMEA, Asia Pacific or Americas groups), otherwise only Dynamics 365 data is used.
  2. Sales Insights settings → Relationship insights → Overview → Enable (turns on analytics and who knows whom) → Save.
  3. Analytics and health: set Activity influence per activity type (values 3–9; the lower the number, the more important), Communication frequency and Health score grading (Good, Fair, Poor; grading can take up to 24 hours).
  4. Who knows whom: pick the email template used for introduction requests.
  • To use who knows whom, a role needs read on wkwcolleaguesforcompany, wkwcolleaguesforcontact and wkwconfig (Salesperson and Sales Manager have access).
  • Custom forms: in the form designer add a column, then Display → Relationship Health or Who Knows Whom; Unified Interface only.
  • Turning relationship analytics off hides scores but health data is still collected. The native Exchange integration for relationship intelligence is deprecated; use server-side synchronization.
Exam traps
  • Activity influence is inverted: 3 outranks 9.
  • Basic needs no setup and Dynamics 365 data only; enhanced adds Exchange data, 24-hour refresh and frequency-plus-recency weighting for who knows whom.
  • Health labels are Good, Fair, Poor — not grades A–D.

Configure Copilot features, including record summarization

Copilot in Dynamics 365 Sales offers chat plus embedded experiences: record summaries (leads, opportunities, accounts), recent changes, SharePoint answers, meeting preparation, email assist and news. It reads only what the signed-in user can access. Microsoft describes the Sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot as the evolution of this experience.

  1. Check prerequisites: supported region; data policies allow the connectors Copilot needs; a Power Platform admin turned Copilot on for Dynamics 365 Sales.
  2. If the region has no Azure OpenAI endpoint, give consent for cross-region data movement in the Power Platform admin center (enable it anyway as a fallback).
  3. Sales Hub → Change area → App Settings → General Settings → Copilot: select Turn audit on (needed for recent changes), set All apps to Default, On or Off and override per app, then Save.
  4. Choose Opportunities, Leads or Accounts and tune the Summary and Recent changes tabs.
Control levelWhere
Tenant: Copilot chat in model-driven apps (marked preview)Power Platform admin center → Copilot → Settings → Power Apps
Tenant: Copilot in Dynamics 365 SalesPower Platform admin center → Copilot → Settings → Dynamics 365 Sales
Entra groupPower Platform admin center → Copilot → Settings → Control who can use AI features in model-driven apps
AppSales Hub → App Settings → Copilot
  • Summary fields: choose at least 4 and at most 15 (recent changes: at most 10) from the table or related tables; Save is disabled outside the range. Customize related info toggles sections such as enriched key info, competitor, product and quote insights, and account leads, opportunities and cases.
  • Recent changes come from audit history: auditing must be on, and sellers need View Audit History and View Audit Summary at organization level.
  • Opportunity widget: select Show opportunity summary as a widget in the form; on custom forms add a 1-column section, then Display → Record summary.
  • For leads handled by the Sales Qualification Agent Copilot always shows the agent's summary (§3.2).
  • Knowledge sources: Copilot → Knowledge sources → Configure SharePoint locations (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, PDF only; SharePoint permissions apply). Email assist: Power Apps app Settings → Features → Contextual email drafting with AI = Yes (lead and opportunity records; no Microsoft 365 Copilot licence needed).
  • Preview Zero prompt experience (customised in Copilot Studio). Deprecated Copilot full-screen view and document summary.
Exam traps
  • The summary-field range is 4–15; recent changes allow only 10.
  • No audit history means no recent-changes list, however many fields you configure.
  • Copilot settings live under App Settings, email assist under Power Apps app features, tenant controls in the Power Platform admin center.
  • Region without an Azure OpenAI endpoint: Copilot stays off until cross-region data movement is accepted.

Configure and use forecasts to help improve sales performance

Forecasts roll opportunity data up a hierarchy for quota tracking. Without any configuration every user sees an out-of-the-box forecast for the current month (org chart based, can't be customised, deleted or deactivated). Configure forecasts under Sales Hub → App Settings → Performance management → Forecast configuration; sellers open them under Performance → Forecasts. Forecasting isn't supported on GCC or mobile devices.

Configuration steps in wizard order:

  1. Select a template: Org chart (rollup Opportunity, hierarchy User via Manager), Product (Opportunity Product, Product) or Territory (Opportunity, Territory); or build from scratch.
  2. Define and schedule: name, rollup entity (only tables with change tracking), hierarchy entity, top of hierarchy and at least one forecast period.
  3. Provide access permissions: owner lookup, additional roles, sharing (None by default, Read-only, Read and adjust).
  4. Configure columns and layout: use the Forecast category option set with Auto-configure.
  5. Configure drill-down entities, then advanced settings (multi-currency, auto-hide parent row, prediction factors).
  6. Activate the forecast and upload data (the simple-column Excel template, for example Quota).
Column typeUse it for
RollupAggregated opportunity values such as Committed or Best Case
CalculatedA formula over other columns
SimpleManually uploaded data such as quota
Hierarchy relatedExtra attributes of the hierarchy entity
  • Limits: at most 50 forecasts, only 6 active; activate only from the configuration page; changes to simple columns can take up to two hours (Microsoft's pages differ on adjustments: one says manager adjustments recalculate immediately, another groups them with the delayed changes, so allow for a delay).
  • Premium forecasting (licence-gated, not in GCC, France or India): needs more than 10 closed opportunities with actual and estimated value and date; add the Prediction column on opportunity-rollup hierarchies, activate, and the values appear in about two hours; enable Prediction factors in Advanced to see drivers.
  • Use: pick forecast and period, check Last updated, use Recalculate data after changing opportunities or the hierarchy. A column must have Allow adjustments before managers can adjust it (direct, indirect and calculated values; Reset restores the calculated value; History tab). You can't adjust rows above your level.
  • Deprecated Forecast snapshots; use the Forecast API. Preview Kanban as default view and default group-by.
Exam traps
  • Quota is a simple column filled by workbook upload, not a rollup.
  • 50 forecasts may exist but only 6 can be active.
  • No pencil icon on a cell: the column lacks Allow adjustments, or the row is above the user's level.
  • The Prediction column appears only when premium forecasting is licensed and available.
  • Sharing is off by default and only a forecast's owner can share it.

Set up goals and goal metrics

Goals are the classic Dataverse goal feature, not an AI feature. A parent goal (for example a region) has child goals (people, teams, territories); a goal has one parent, the parent total is the sum of its children, and deleting a parent doesn't delete the children. Rollups run bottom to top.

To trackGoal metric
Number of calls made or leads createdCount (integer)
RevenueAmount → Money
Units soldAmount → Integer
A product sold by weightAmount → Decimal
  1. Goal metric: App Settings → Performance management → Goal Metrics → New. Choose Metric Type (Count = integer; Amount = Money, Integer or Decimal). Type and data type can't change after saving. Tick Track Stretch Target if needed.
  2. Rollup fields: at least one, never two of the same type: Actual, In-progress, Custom Rollup Field. Each names a source record type (custom types aren't supported), source field, state, status and the date field that decides the goal period.
  3. Rollup query (optional): Performance management → Rollup Queries; one entity type; use real values, not dynamic values such as Current User; at most 5,000 records are counted.
  4. Goal: Performance → Goals → New: name, optional parent (then metric and time period are copied and locked), metric, owner, Time Period (fiscal or custom), Targets (plus stretch target), Goal Criteria (roll up only from child goals; record set Owned by goal owner or All; rollup queries for Actual and In-Progress), then Recalculate.
  • Rollup schedule (Goals Settings, System Administrator or Customizer): recurrence 24 hours by default and never lower; rollup stops 30 days after the goal end date by default; manual recalculation is always possible.
  • After a fiscal-year change use Align with Fiscal Period on the goal.
  • Don't confuse goal targets with forecast quotas: quotas are a simple column in a forecast.
Exam traps
  • Metric type and amount data type are permanent once saved; create a new metric instead.
  • A child goal inherits metric and time period from its parent and can't change them.
  • Rollup queries ignore dynamic filter values such as Current User or Last X Days.
  • Goal rollups can't run more often than every 24 hours; use Recalculate for an immediate update.
